extension.summary: Standalone Stremio-style catalog/stream client for Kodi with TMDb Helper integration, Plex/Emby/Silo sources, Trakt PIN linking and scrobble.
عميل مستقل لكتالوجات وروابط Stremio داخل Kodi مع دعم مشغّل TMDb Helper ومصادر Plex وEmby وSilo وربط Trakt عبر PIN.
extension.description: Standalone Dex Hub for Kodi. Add compatible Stremio manifests, browse provider catalogs, use native Plex, Emby/Jellyfin and Silo sources, play streams with external subtitles, link Trakt, reuse Dex Hub as a TMDb Helper player, and keep a unified local continue-watching list.

Dex Hub نسخة مستقلة لـ Kodi. أضف روابط Stremio، واستخدم مصادر Plex وEmby/Jellyfin وSilo الأصلية، وشغّل الترجمات الخارجية، واربط Trakt، واستخدم Dex Hub كمشغّل لـ TMDb Helper، وحافظ على قائمة متابعة موحّدة محلياً.
extension.disclaimer: The author of this addon does not host any of the content which is found and has no affiliation with any of the content providers. The author is in no way affiliated with Kodi, Team Kodi, or the XBMC Foundation.
مؤلّف هذه الإضافة لا يستضيف أيًّا من المحتوى الذي يتم العثور عليه، وليس له أي ارتباط بأي من مزوّدي المحتوى. لا يرتبط المؤلّف بأي شكل مع Kodi أو فريق Kodi أو مؤسّسة XBMC.
extension.news: 5.10.592: When Google Translate says it is busy (too many requests from your connection), Dex Hub moves to Google's second address for ten minutes instead of failing; a translation service you pick still applies when it cannot be saved. 5.10.591: On a Silo title, Translate subtitle uses the service you chose; Silo's own AI translation is a choice in the button's list, under Google and AI. 5.10.590: The Translate subtitle button shows its services when it has the focus, as the Subtitles button shows its subtitles (with skin 3.28.232): Google Translate, DexWorld and each AI service you set up with its model, the one in use checked; pick one to translate with it, and it stays chosen. The button now shows in everyone's player bar, which has a tenth slot in skin 3.28.232. An embedded subtitle's translation shows sooner: a smaller first part (48 lines), the file's index read once, a refused line asked again instead of stopping. A disc's subtitle syncs again with DexSubtitles installed (Dex Hub has its own sync queue now). 5.10.589: A Blu-ray disc image from Debrid or Usenet opens a little sooner (its size comes with the first check), and a disc played again opens without reading its file system again, even by a new link; AI metadata translation also translates the story a title page shows from its catalog when TMDb gave none, and the log says why a story was not translated. 5.10.588: Translate subtitle: the playing subtitle, embedded (text tracks of an MKV, read line by line from the file's index, never the video) or external, translated into your subtitle language with Google Translate, DexWorld or an AI service, the timing kept, the minutes around you first (on in seconds, the rest after; nothing in 25 s cancels it); a player bar button (Player buttons, with skin.dexhub 3.28.231). AI is a Control Centre section of its own: search, recommendations and lists, subtitle translation and the new metadata translation (a story TMDb has only in another language) each with its own service and model (free ones marked), services and keys once (DexWorld, Claude and Mistral join; any OpenAI-compatible address, http too), and what each sends. A Silo source keeps the Silo server's own AI translation. With DexSubtitles installed, a Blu-ray disc's subtitle syncs again (Dex Hub keeps discs; DexSubtitles cannot read them). 5.10.587: Usenet: a release that fails no longer hands the player its NZB link (it goes to the next source), a release that does not open says why in plain words (provider not reached, its connections in use, no NZB from the indexer...), with the engine's own reason in the log (Usenet engine 1.3.2); a new film missing its year is looked up on TMDb so its name search runs. 5.10.586: LibreELEC: the library index works without SQLite FTS5; Usenet finds more of a new film (by IMDb and by name), reads a second page, keeps no empty answer and names the Prowlarr indexers that are paused; a second Usenet release waits for the first to open; Kodi no longer hangs on closing because of Dex Hub (its disc server and a start-up timer stopped it, and a late service missed the stop); an add-on link with http stays http. 5.10.585: The subtitle panel in the player is wider and shows each subtitle's whole name (the chosen one grows up to four lines), file names with dots wrap instead of being cut; Usenet plays on LibreELEC and Linux PCs with Intel or AMD chips (with the Usenet engine 1.3.1). 5.10.584: A stopped disc no longer freezes Kodi for minutes (disc images are served by a process of their own), Java disc menus with their pictures in a folder show (The Uprising stayed black), a subtitle picked inside a disc's film stays on it, the Disc menu button goes back without the Home in between, trailers no longer freeze Kodi or stop on a row refresh, and Usenet releases from Prowlarr are sorted by quality and size. 5.10.583: Usenet: a Prowlarr is one entry for all its Usenet indexers (one search, each release under its indexer's name), the engine starts while you choose and stays 30 minutes, and Retry asks the indexers again. 5.10.582: Usenet: releases with a password show (the engine opens many, whole Blu-ray discs among them), an indexer is not asked the same search again for half an hour, late indexers no longer lose their releases, and the provider test trusts what the engine trusts. 5.10.581: Blu-ray discs over the internet open in their menus much sooner (the Batman from Emby: 93 s to 27 s), the Disc menu button in the player bar takes you back to the disc's main menu, subtitle sync works on discs, a trailer starts at once on the card you are on and a trailer that does not answer is left out quietly, and Dex Hub says where it carries a title on from. 5.10.580: Kodi 22: a disc set to "Show Blu-ray menu" opens on its menu again (Dex Hub read it as "Play main movie" and opened the film). 5.10.579: Groq joins the AI services (Control Centre › AI). 5.10.578: A new row goes right after Continue Watching at the top of the page, even when Next episode is further down. 5.10.577: A row you add (an AI list, a list, a Kodi path, Add to Home) goes above the row you were on, or at the top under Continue Watching, not at the end; hidden rows no longer count toward the 120-row limit. 5.10.576: AI with your own key (Grok, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, DeepSeek): search by description, Home rows made from a description, and Recommended for you from what you watched; Basic settings now show DexCloud, Debrid, EasyNews, backups and the player's buttons; new option: a Blu-ray without your subtitle language opens on the film with the subtitle file, no second start. 5.10.575: Any Kodi path as a Home row: Edit Home, Add rows, From Kodi (video sources, the library, playlists, or a path you type). 5.10.574: The sources themes in Aura's colours (all but Classic), each its own layout: Poster (the poster and plot), Aura, Halo (coloured badges) and Prism (full details). 5.10.573: The Telegram bot answers (DexCloud hub 2.18): search and play on the TV from it, your Continue watching, Next episode, watch history and Home lists, all in Dex Hub's look. 5.10.572: Whole Blu-ray discs from Usenet play (a COMPLETE.BLURAY release is a disc image in a password-protected archive; with the Usenet engine 1.3.0 it opens) and open as a disc in Kodi; a Blu-ray image (.iso) from any Debrid or add-on link plays on the Mac, Apple TV, Android and Windows too, where Kodi hung or could not read one: Dex Hub reads the image over the internet and hands Kodi its disc folder; a disc with Java menus (most UHD discs) opens on its main film instead of stopping in its menu, a disc with plain menus opens in them, and on CoreELEC and LibreELEC (Java menus run there) every disc opens in its menu; Kodi's "Play main movie" setting is followed; a subtitle switched on in a disc's menus from any add-on plays the main film from the same place with it at once, no question, and stays; Dex Hub picks no subtitle itself in a disc's menus. 5.10.571: Whole Blu-ray discs from TorBox open in their own menus (intros, menu, chapters, languages; the film starts from the menu); StremThru Torz joins the built-in torrent sites, with new addresses for YTS, TorrentGalaxy, Zilean, MediaFusion and Comet; one row per release when it was uploaded under several hashes; a ready torrent with no video inside (a fake .exe, an archive) is no longer offered; an indexer that refuses a Usenet search says why; a TorBox torrent added only to play it is removed again when nothing of it plays. 5.10.570: Only torrent sources that work today: every well-known public add-on (Torrentio, Comet, Peerflix, MediaFusion, Meteor, TorrentsDB, Knightcrawler) is tried with a real search before it is added, looked at again weekly, and replaced or removed when it stops; the built-in sites try their other addresses and step aside for 30 minutes when none answers. 5.10.569: Built-in torrent scrapers (YTS, EZTV, TheRARBG, TorrentGalaxy, The Pirate Bay, Knaben, Zilean) asked together from this device, Peerflix added with Torrentio and Comet; a full Kodi backup, a backup of all of Kodi's settings, or Dex Hub alone, with a restore for each. 5.10.568: Debrid of its own: link Real-Debrid, AllDebrid or TorBox with a QR from your phone (Premiumize with its key), and torrents from Torrentio, Comet, any Stremio add-on, CocoScrapers or your own Debrid files play straight from your account; Torrentio and Comet are added for you, ready ones are marked, and no POV, Fen Light, Umbrella or Red Light is needed. 5.10.567: Blu-ray and DVD images: subtitle files work again (a disc opened at its resume point went to its menus, where they never show); Dex Hub keeps the disc's own subtitle in its menus and offers to play the main movie from the same place. 5.10.566: Mark intro in the player (where TheIntroDB has none, the season's other episodes skip it); SMB and NFS shares are named as such in Servers; the NAS search says in the log why it was not searched; turn an add-on off and on again from its menu, without removing it. 5.10.565: The sources page reads the plot in Arabic and the ratings for titles from a Nuvio profile's catalogs too (they stayed English), Classic shows two whole lines of plot, and Kodi's mounted video folders (CoreELEC, LibreELEC) join the NAS source. 5.10.564: The YouTube page laid out as the YouTube TV app: its side rail (Search, Home, Shorts, Music, Subscriptions, Library, Live, Gaming, Sports, News, Settings), its own shelves in its order, Shorts as tall cards, a SoundCloud-style music player with its queue, and a queue of videos no longer plays behind the page. 5.10.563: IPTV films and episodes, and YouTube videos, open the player again (they played behind the page); several server addresses per IPTV source, tried in turn; a provider's 5xx is asked once more and its own codes (like HTTP 513) explained. 5.10.562: The Aura sources page shows its ratings whole (no chip cut at the panel edge) and the plot in Arabic when the metadata language is Arabic. 5.10.561: NAS section titles play their NAS file directly from the title page, with the NAS file listed in Sources. 5.10.560: The Aura sources theme (default); IPTV films and series open the title page and play the provider file directly, with it listed in Sources; Xtream VOD plays again; DexWorld lists and playback from the provider when its server is blocked; Info on server Continue Watching items; a new default look. 5.10.559: Usenet on Apple TV: the engine now lives inside the Dex Hub Apple TV app itself, and the engine add-on starts it when a Usenet source is picked. 5.10.558: Usenet as a source of its own: your NNTP provider and Newznab indexers (Settings, Sources, Usenet), played on this device through a separate engine program (Mac and CoreELEC). 5.10.557: the source filter as a side panel with TRaSH Guides chips, the sources come back when nothing plays, EasyNews as a source, a subtitle from a file.
